text: Given valid credential headers and object_class="Incidents", when alloy_list_objects is called with limit=10, then it returns a JSON array of at most 10 incident objects containing the requested fields.
Given a search_text that matches nothing, when alloy_list_objects is called, then it returns an empty objects array, not an error.
Given a known oid, when alloy_get_object is called, then it returns that single object's detail fields.
Given a known oid, when alloy_get_object_activities is called, then it returns that object's activity/history entries in order.
Given a classification/dictionary name, when alloy_get_dictionary is called, then it returns that classification's code-to-label values.

Given a /mcp request missing one of the three required credential headers, when any tool is called, then the service returns HTTP 401 naming the missing header(s), and Alloy Navigator is never called.

Given an object_class Alloy Navigator rejects (e.g. an unknown class name), when alloy_list_objects is called, then it returns the structured error envelope with code="invalid_argument", not an unhandled exception.
Given an oid that does not exist, when alloy_get_object is called, then it returns the structured error envelope with code="not_found".

Given two concurrent requests carrying two different tenants' credential headers, when both are in flight at the same time, then each outbound call to Alloy Navigator uses only its own request's credentials, never the other tenant's.

Given Alloy Navigator returns a 5xx or the connection times out, when any tool is called, then it returns the structured error envelope with code="upstream_error" and retryable=true, not an unhandled exception or a hang.

Given a real tenant's Alloy Navigator credentials, when an Agent is asked a representative ITSM question spanning more than one tool (e.g. list open incidents for a computer and show the last 3 activity entries), then it selects and chains the right tools using only their descriptions, and the results match what the tenant's own Alloy Navigator console shows.
steps: Register a real tenant's X-Alloy-Base-Url / X-Alloy-Client-Id / X-Alloy-Client-Secret against the deployed service
Open the tenant's Alloy Navigator console and note a handful of real incidents/computers for comparison
In an Agent session with this connector attached, ask: 'List open incidents for computer <name> and show the last 3 activity entries for the most recent one'
Observe which tools the Agent calls and compare the returned data to the console
expect: The Agent calls alloy_list_objects(object_class="Incidents", ...) then alloy_get_object_activities on the right oid, purely from the tool descriptions, and the returned incidents/activities match the tenant's console for the same filter
evidence: needs a real Alloy Navigator vendor account; not available at design/dev time (mcp-track.md 2.5: absence does not block delivery)
